justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.descrip: Five 5″ frames with equal parts: the arms make the difference
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.step.de: The camera sits far ahead of the spread front arms. That keeps the props out of the camera image – ideal for footage.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.step.hf: Two long rails carry the motors, the camera sits far forward. No props in view, but more mass and drag.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.step.li: Seen from above: all five 5″ drones carry the same motors, props, batteries and cameras. Only the arm layout differs.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.step.sq: The other way round: wider than long. Flips come quicker than rolls. Many freestyle pilots like exactly that.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.step.st: The motors sit further forward and back than sideways. Rolls get snappier, flips slower. Built slim, the frame is faster in a straight line.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.frames.title: Frame shapes compared
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.callou: Share code: the build as text
Tuning and paint straight onto the drone
Part missing? It is on the shopping list
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.descri: Share codes: pass on build, paint and tuning as text
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.step.e: In the workbench, “Share code” shows the finished build as short text. “Copy to clipboard” takes paint, tuning and name along.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.step.h: In the configurator tab “Share code” you apply only tuning or paint to the drone in your hand. Paint costs dyes.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.step.i: On “Import” you see a preview, flight stats and a part check. “Apply” fills the workbench, in creative with new parts.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.step.s: In survival the parts come from your inventory. Whatever is missing shows up on the shopping list – nothing is free.
justmoreparts.guide.scene.sharing.title: Sharing builds
